Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Brandon King and Alick Athanaze are the two openers for the West Indies. Hasan Mahmud has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... TUN RUN CHASE ...
So, will the West Indies complete a clean sweep, or can Bangladesh secure a consolation victory? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned as we will be back with West Indies' reply in a short while...

Alzarri Joseph is in for a quick chat. He says that it was a good effort and the wicket was conducive to batting. Says that their intention was to take early wickets, which they successfully achieved. Adds that he has confidence in his team's ability to chase down the target and that they just need a couple of good partnerships.

The West Indies had an early opportunity to dismiss Soumya, but failed to do so and it costed them. Although they managed to remove both Soumya and Mehidy shortly after, the West Indies struggled to penetrate further into the batting lineup. Alzarri Joseph was their pick of the bowlers as he chipped two wickets and was very much economical. Roston Chase was economical too but was wicketless. The rest of their bowler leaked runs. Now, they face a challenging target for the chase.

Bangladesh end with a mammoth 321 on board and they will be the happier side going into the break. They were off to a shaky start but ended well. Mahmudullah and Jaker formed a formidable partnership, remaining unbeaten with a stand of 140 runs, which allowed them to capitalize on the solid start provided by the top order. Soumya and Mehidy both contributed significantly with fluent half-centuries.
Ends with a dot! Too full, outside off, Mahmudullah looks to play at it but misses. Bangladesh end their innings at 321/5!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Tanzid Hasan and Soumya Sarkar are the two openers for Bangladesh. Alzarri Joseph has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Soumya Sarkar, Litton Das (WK), Mehidy Hasan (C), Afif Hossain, Mahmudullah, Jaker Ali, Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed (In for Nahid Rana), Hasan Mahmud (In for Shoriful Islam), Nasum Ahmed (In for Tanzim Hasan Sakib).

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Alick Athanaze (In for Justin Greaves), Keacy Carty, Shai Hope (C)(WK), Sherfane Rutherford, Roston Chase, Romario Shepherd, Amir Jangoo (In for Evin Lewis), Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph (In for Jayden Seales), Jediah Blades (In for Marquino Mindley).
Mehidy Hasan says they'll be looking to bat better! Adds they'll need close to 300. Adds it is learning phase for them and the boys have backed him. Informs they have three changes.
Shai Hope says they prefer chasing and hence want to chase. Informs they have a few forced changes. Adds they need to adapt to the conditions and do well.
TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and ELECTED TO BOWL!

With the series advantage in hand, the West Indies will aim for another strong performance! Will Bangladesh find a way to turn the tide, or will the West Indies continue their dominance? Join us for all the action in a short while. Toss and team news in a bit...

In the previous outings, Bangladesh struggled to defend their totals, being bowled out for 227 in the last match despite some fighting performances from Tanzid Hasan and Mahmudullah. The West Indies showcased their batting prowess, with Brandon King leading his brilliant batting, supported well by Evin Lewis and Keacy Carty. On the other hand, Bangladesh will be upset with their performance and will look to walks back with a win.

Hello and a warm welcome to the third and the final ODI of the Bangladesh tour of West Indies. Having already clinched the series, the Men in Maroon will be looking to complete a full sweep with another emphatic victory.
... MATCH DAY ...

Bangladesh's tour of West Indies continues and after a 1-1 draw in the Test series, hosts West Indies have gone and clinched the three-match ODI series 2-0 with a game in hand. Next up is the 3rd ODI between West Indies and Bangladesh to be played at Warner Park in Basseterre, St Kitts once again before we finally move to Kingstown in St. Vincent for the T20I series. Game 1 of the ODI series began with a lot of promise and the sides looked very well-matched just like how the Test series ended but the duo of Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford helped the Windies chase down 295 runs and this resulted in a big confidence boost. The hosts were all over Bangladesh in the 2nd game and cruised to a series win. Bangladesh will be looking to bounce back and even though they are without a few big guns, they need to have the self-belief to go on and get things done. After an underwhelming showing from the top order in the first game, West Indies' top three batters found their groove in a sub-par chase with Brandon King really coming into his own. The likes of Evin Lewis and Keacy Carty too got useful runs under their belt but the job was set up brilliantly in the first innings by the bowlers. Riding high on Jayden Seales' four-fer, the hosts kept Bangladesh to under 230 runs which was more than 60 runs less in the first game at the same venue. For Bangladesh, it was a case of no one really taking the mantle on their own and the experience of Mahmudullah along with a very handy knock from Tanzim Hasan Sakib down the order saved them from what could have been a really low total. Still, though, their batting performance was under-par and the bowlers never managed to get in the game, thanks to some counter-attack from the Windies openers from the get-go. Bangladesh really need to pull up their socks and find their lost mojo in this format of the game, where they usually shine the brightest but it will be tough without some very key players and an upbeat Windies side as well. Can Bangladesh avoid the clean sweep? Or will West Indies rally along to a 3-0 victory? We shall find out.
